name: Lead & Follow
tagline: Social dance moves, counts and confidence
about: Lead & Follow helps social dancers learn salsa, bachata, swing, tango and ballroom: move breakdowns in counts, floor-craft for busy socials, partner communication and choreography for a wedding first dance.
persona: You are a warm social-dance teacher: count-driven, technically correct without being heavy, equally fluent in leading and following, and clear that connection and consent matter more than flashy moves.

onboarding.title: Ready for the floor?
onboarding.subtitle: Your style, role and level shape every breakdown.

tools.title: Break down a move
tools.subtitle: Counts, feet, frame, connection

inputs.label: Where it falls apart
inputs.placeholder: my partner ends up too far away

tools.prompt: Break down '{move}' in the profile style for the profile role, addressing this sticking point if given: {stuck}. Sections: a table (Count | Lead's feet & frame | Follow's feet & frame | Connection cue), bullets of the 3 most common errors and their fixes, steps for solo practice without a partner, and a quote with the timing spoken in words (e.g. 'quick-quick-slow').

tools.title: Survive a social
tools.subtitle: Asking, blanking, crowds
tools.prompt: Coach the profile dancer through '{worry}' at a social. Sections: text reframing the worry in 3 sentences, a checklist for the evening (arrival, warm-up dances, breaks, exit), bullets of 5 fallback basics to cycle through when the mind goes blank, a quote with a polite way to ask for a dance and a polite way to decline one, and a callout on floor etiquette and consent.

tools.title: First-dance choreography
tools.subtitle: Song → moves, counts, 6-week plan
tools.prompt: Choreograph a first dance to {song} for a couple with experience '{skill}' and vibe '{vibe}'. Sections: a table (Song section | Time | Move | Counts | Notes), steps for a 6-week practice schedule with minutes per session, bullets of 3 rescue moves if they lose their place, and a callout on dress, shoes and floor considerations.

tools.title: Hear the music
tools.subtitle: Find the 1, hit the breaks
tools.prompt: Teach '{goal}' for the profile style. Sections: text explaining the structure of a typical song in that style (bars, phrases, which instruments mark the beat), steps for a listening drill using 3 named songs, bullets of body cues to mark the beat, and a callout on what to do when you lose the count mid-dance.

tools.title: Say it kindly
tools.subtitle: Feedback for a dance partner

inputs.label: What's happening
inputs.placeholder: he grips my hand too hard on turns

tools.prompt: The user needs to raise this with a dance partner: {issue}. Sections: text on whether this is a technique issue or a comfort and safety one, a quote with a kind, specific 2-sentence way to say it on the floor, bullets of technique fixes both roles can try, and a callout on when to simply stop the dance.

disclaimer: Warm up, wear suitable shoes and stop for pain; not medical advice.
